results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 75 aligned units' outline summaries state the controlling idea of their aligned spec paragraph (p01 to p74, including p22a and p57 to p59 and p53 to p56 in their declared positions), in the spec's order; the five intro callouts match no spec paragraph and carry the roadmap and thesis as the spec's introduction places them.

The outliner marked KEY POINTS callout, Introduction ¶3, Architecture ¶13, Worked Example ¶6 and ¶7 as holding two ideas. In each case the pair is the single controlling idea the spec declares for that unit (p03: the two terms and the case they are applied to; p42: 'two design rules keep the seams honest'; p48: write load and value inversely distributed, so cost models are read against the profile; p49: the cars and jobs sections classified by their profiles); the KEY POINTS callout is the declared three-bullet thesis carrier. No unit holds an idea outside its spec paragraph.

Every body unit serves one of V1 to V5: scene and concepts set up V1/V2; differ, in-practice and who-decides support V1; architecture supports V2 to V4; trade-offs V2/V5; worked example V1, V2, V4, V5; failure modes and Chief Architect's view V3 to V5; conclusion restates the thesis. No orphan paragraph found.

Each table is introduced and its caption states what it shows, and the following prose draws the consequence (Table 1 by Concepts ¶4, Table 2 by the three-row subsections, Table 3 by Who Decides ¶3, Table 4 by Architecture ¶6, Table 5 by Trade-offs ¶3 and ¶4, Table 6 by Worked Example ¶3, Table 7 by ¶6, Table 8 by ¶10). Figures 2 and 3 are explained in Architecture ¶1, ¶9 and ¶12; Figures 1 and 4 sit with paragraphs that state their point. Quotations (AVIV, Adevinta, Rightmove, Google, Indeed, Vinted) are each followed by what they show, with stated limits ('What the integrated platform contained is not public', 'The record does not say how much of the unified platform shipped').

Each section and paragraph transition_in is expressed at its boundary: e.g. scene 'It is mid-March 2027' (sequence), concepts 'To turn Ingrid's answers into profiles' (elaboration), in-practice 'The row sections above cited the record one dimension at a time' (additional_support), who-decides 'The public record also shows' (additional_support), architecture 'Verticals differ, outside parties rewrite their requirements ... so' (cause_effect), trade-offs 'The four layers are one answer; a group could choose others' (contrast), chief-architect 'Each of these failures starts as an undecided or unwatched question' (problem_solution), questions 'Turn those decisions and signals' (conclusion_summary), conclusion 'This chapter opened with the synergy case's question' (conclusion_summary); paragraph-level transitions likewise. Introduction ¶3 ('This chapter owns two terms') and Concepts ¶5 state the cause/sequence only implicitly through their definitions; judged acceptable. The failure-modes opening expresses the declared elaboration but is hard to follow (recorded under flow_is_followable).

results.quote: The chapter starts at Veldmark's March 2027 workshop, on one platform for four verticals. It then defines the two terms, compares five verticals on the profile
results.finding: Both flow readers had to work out which 'four' is meant: the opening uses four for Veldmark's brands ('all four Veldmark brands', Introduction ¶1) and for its verticals (heading, roadmap), then the chapter compares five verticals, and nowhere says that recommerce is the one Veldmark does not run (the AC-2 cold reader raised the same question). The spec's order is fine; one clause naming the four Veldmark verticals and why a fifth is compared would remove it.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: What the Public Record Shows ¶1
results.quote: The row sections above cited the record one dimension at a time. Read vertical by vertical, it shows how physics shapes whole systems, and how often groups reversed what they shared.
results.finding: Both flow readers felt they were re-reading evidence: In Practice cites again the sources the row subsections just used (mobile.de Seller API, Rightmove RTDF, Pkw-EnVKV) and both suggest cutting it to what is new or merging it with the rows. The repetition follows from the spec's structure (decision log: fourteen-dimension rows followed by per-vertical 'In Practice' evidence, with p23 and p32 evidence reusing p17 and p20 sources), not from the prose.

results.quote: The four layers are one answer; a group could choose others. Groups choose among four broad options for supporting several verticals. The share test is a way of mixing them per capability
results.finding: Both flow readers stopped to keep four layers and four options apart and to map one onto the other; the mapping (B = layers 1 and 2 shared, D = how a layer-3 capability reaches other brands) becomes clear only later. Both readers judged the section's position sound; a mapping sentence at the opening would fix it.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Three Listings, Three Physics ¶1
results.quote: Over the spring, Ingrid's team checks them against three later listings this book follows through Parts II and III (Table 6).
results.finding: Both flow readers re-read the dates: Table 6 dates the Rotterdam bike to Sunday 7 March 2027, before the mid-March workshop, so not all three listings are 'later'. The spec's controlling idea for p43 itself says 'the three later listings', so the error is in the spec as well as the draft.

results.draft_locus: Veldmark Worked Example: Three Listings, Three Physics ¶8
results.quote: In March the workshop drafted a first shared-versus-specific table for the Common Ground capability list. Table 8 is the version the architecture advice forum, the open weekly forum for cross-brand decisions, ratifies in April 2027; the Lyon apartment, listed in May, tests it rather than shapes it.
results.finding: Both flow readers could not tell which listings produced the profiles and which tested them: the section announces the result first, moves to spring listings, goes back to the March workshop's work on Tradeyard Poland's sections, then to the March draft, April ratification and May test; it also sits uneasily with the scene, where each brand's one real listing becomes the first profile (reader B). Both propose a chronological order. The difficulty comes from the spec's declared small_to_large order for this section and from p43 versus p07 in the spec, not from the sentences.

results.quote: Felix's gate guards against one way option B decays; this is the first of six.
results.finding: Both flow readers re-read this bridge: it is unclear what 'one way' and 'this' refer to (reader A), and the previous section said B decays into A or C, while profiling only the largest vertical is not obviously either (reader B). The spec's elaboration (gate, then six failure modes) is sound; the prose should say that an engine built for the largest vertical is the Forced Fit, the route by which B drifts toward A, and that six failure modes follow.

results.quote: [[bounded-contexts]] decided that one context owns the listing's truth, and this chapter showed items whose identities and systems of record sit outside the listing.
results.finding: Both flow readers read the two halves of the hand-off as an unreconciled contradiction. The spec's hand_off pairs them but they are compatible (the context owns the listing; the item's identity and the source record are referenced from outside); the prose joins them with 'and' and never says how they fit, so the fix is a reconciling clause.

results.quote: Keybridge, its software business for agencies, lists nothing itself.
results.finding: Reader A: a dangling fact in the introduction that pays off only in Table 8's caption.

results.quote: I use fourteen dimensions, grouped by the part of the architecture they stress
results.finding: Reader A: the first-person 'I' arrives straight after narrative about Ingrid, so it is unclear whether it is Ingrid or the author.

results.quote: The profile records them, and the architecture has to be ready for their changes.
results.finding: Reader B: none of the fourteen dimensions is 'outside parties', so it is unclear whether this adds a fifteenth dimension or which row records them. The spec's controlling idea says 'the profile records them', so the cause is unclear.

results.quote: The automotive row needs one comment. After retailer pushback, Autotrader paused the automatic rollout of Deal Builder

results.quote: **Missing a regulatory field as a feature gap.**
results.finding: Reader B: the heading is ambiguous (it means treating a missing mandatory field as a feature gap).

Reader A (minor): 'price rating' is used before it is explained (In Practice ¶2). The failure-pattern names both readers found undefined (Ghost Inventory, Deal-Shaped Architecture, Seeing Double) are on the audience's already_knows list and are not counted; every does_not_know term visible in the prose is given at first use (DMS, MLS, applicant tracking system, type-approval codes hsn/tsn, DPE, ESCO, O*NET; VIN as a 17-character identity).

The introduction opens with the declared thought-provoking question and bridge from Part I's maps, states the thesis (KEY POINTS, ¶2, ¶3) and gives a roadmap (callout and ¶4); no weak pattern (dictionary opening, throat-clearing, announcement without stakes).
The conclusion answers the opening question, draws the consequence for a group and ends with a concrete course of action and hand-off; it is not a bare summary or a new-topic ending.

From Physics to Models ¶1 synthesizes ('no for the listing model and yes for the machinery beneath it', ending in one share test of four layers); ¶2 answers so what with the April 2027 ratified table and Motorvane's gated move, and gives the takeaway to write numbered profiles and place every capability part in a layer with an owner and reason.

¶1 returns to the opening question verbatim in substance ('can one listing platform, with a category tree per vertical, carry a used sofa, a family car, an apartment and a job?') and ¶2 to Part I's opening claim that the business decides the architecture, as the spec's callback declares.

The cold reader of the opening alone predicted the exact section order the roadmap promises (scene; profile and share decision; five-vertical comparison; public record; outside parties; platform with vertical seams in four layers; pure strategies; three Veldmark listings and the workshop's classification; failure modes; Chief Architect's view; review questions; hand-off to Part II) and the kinds of evidence (dated public record, fictional Veldmark). Its only hesitation, four versus five verticals, is recorded under flow_is_followable.

The cold reader answered as expected: the plan should not decide; the move is a stage gate on the car vertical's requirement profile measured by Motorvane's own feed success rate and delete latency; dealer-feed adapters and the vehicle schema are vertical (layer-2) content on shared engines; vehicle identity, specification decoding and price rating are a layer-3 capability with one owner, offered to other brands by contract.
